grounds.point: Canara Bank sublet or otherwise parted with possession of portions of the premises to Respondents 2 to 6.
grounds.explanation: The landlord alleged that Respondents 2 to 6 paid amounts to Canara Bank, held portions exclusively, and that Canara Bank retained no portion; the respondents admitted their use of portions but characterized the arrangements as licences and asserted that Canara Bank retained legal possession. The supplied record does not contain a resolving finding on the disputed possession sufficient to determine independently whether these arrangements amounted to subletting or parting with possession under section 14(1)(b).

grounds.point: The Addl. Rent Controller found that the landlord had consented to the sub-tenancy on the basis of the lease deed and rent-related documents.
grounds.explanation: The appellant's own ground of challenge identifies the prior court's holding that Respondent No. 1 inducted Respondents 2 to 6 pursuant to the lease deed and rent receipt and that the documents showed the landlord's consent; Respondent No. 1 likewise identifies the finding that acceptance of increased rent reflected consent. That identified prior-court finding must be preserved at that level even though the target appellate court's final reasoning is withheld.

grounds.point: The consent identified by the prior court satisfied section 14(1)(b)'s requirement of previous consent in writing.
grounds.explanation: Section 14(1)(b) requires consent in writing. The respondents relied on the 1944 lease deed and a 1977 voucher and the prior court found consent, while the appellant contended that the lease instead required separate previous written permission and that the voucher had been misread; the supplied target record does not reproduce the operative clause or voucher language sufficiently to resolve that statutory qualification independently.

grounds.point: The original Pratap Bank tenancy passed through amalgamations to Lakshmi Commercial Bank in 1961 and Canara Bank in 1985.
grounds.explanation: The allowed record states that Pratap Bank, the original 1944 tenant, amalgamated with Lakshmi Commercial Bank with effect from 10.12.1961 and that Lakshmi Commercial Bank was later amalgamated into Canara Bank with effect from 23.08.1985. These transfers occurred after the statutory date in section 14(1)(b), but their legal consequence still depends on the supplied law and the written-consent requirement.

grounds.point: The two bank amalgamations independently establish a prohibited assignment or parting with possession under Delhi Rent Control Act section 14(1)(b).
grounds.explanation: The reported Parasaram passage states broadly that Delhi section 14(b) reaches assignment and other modes of parting with possession, including an involuntary sale, while General Radio treated a company-proposed court-sanctioned amalgamation as a transfer under the distinct Andhra Pradesh statute. Telesound's Delhi amalgamation discussion was expressly prima facie and reserved the section 14(1)(b) eviction question, and the target record supplies neither the legal mechanism of these bank amalgamations nor a resolving fact about written landlord consent to them; the supplied authorities therefore do not establish this independent eviction path.

grounds.point: Notice under section 17 is an additional necessary element of the landlord's fixed eviction ground under section 14(1)(b).
grounds.explanation: The supplied text of section 14(1)(b) makes the fixed ground depend on subletting, assignment or parting with possession without written landlord consent. Section 17 separately addresses notice where premises have been sublet with previous written consent, and section 18 governs consequences for qualifying sub-tenants after an eviction order; the supplied provisions do not make section 17 notice an additional element of the landlord's section 14(1)(b) ground.

reason: The allowed record preserves a prior finding of landlord consent but does not permit an independent resolution of whether the disputed occupations involved statutory subletting or parting with possession and whether the identified consent satisfied the required previous written-consent condition. The separate amalgamation theory also remains unresolved under the limited Delhi authorities and target consent facts supplied, so the fixed section 14(1)(b) ground cannot be established or definitively rejected on this record. 粘贴的文本 (1)
